rounds.text: Ansal Properties & Infrastructure Ltd presents a precarious financial profile defined by severe long-term revenue erosion and a balance sheet in distress. The company’s compounded sales growth has been negative over both the 10-year and 5-year periods [E11, E12, E48], culminating in a catastrophic 70% decline in sales over the trailing twelve months [E14] and a 92% year-over-year drop [E55]. This persistent inability to generate top-line growth is compounded by a negative book value of ₹ -115, which renders traditional valuation metrics like price-to-book essentially meaningless [E1]. Furthermore, the company fails to return capital to shareholders, evidenced by a dividend yield of 0.00% [E3]. The business is also failing to utilize its assets effectively, as shown by an ROA of -2.74% compared to the sector benchmark of 1.44% [E7]. Conceded: the company shows a high ROE of 37.1% [E8], profit growth exceeding 20% YoY [E52], and recent quarterly sales improvement [E54]. Despite these isolated positive signals, the broader evidence suggests that market expectations are running significantly ahead of actual delivery, with price growth outpacing profit growth by 531% [E44].
